Subject: Downstream vendor consent required for Cloudline integration

Hi Tessa,

We're moving forward with the Cloudline integration for the Analytics pilot (SOW attached). Legal on their side flagged that Cloudline will subcontract a small telemetry processor (EdgeStream) that will handle aggregated logs. They asked us to confirm Redwood's vendor flow-down terms — specifically:

- Authorization to subcontract (yes/no)
- Minimum DPA clauses to flow down (data access, retention, incident notification windows)
- Any audit/evidence requirements (SOC 2, penetration test reports)

Can you confirm our stance so I can provide a single consolidated response to Cloudline? We've attached the SOW and a proposed vendor matrix for reference.

Thanks,
Clara Hsu
Sr. Procurement Manager, EnterpriseCo

Subject: Re: Downstream vendor consent required for Cloudline integration

Hi Clara — thanks for the heads up and the materials. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Dev (Engineering) to confirm scope and required evidence. Preliminary notes from my side:

- Redwood permits subcontracting with prior notification for low-risk telemetry processors, but we require flow-down of core DPA obligations (confidentiality, limited use, breach notification).
- For anything that processes customer data beyond aggregated telemetry (i.e., any PII or identifiers), we require written approval + specific technical controls.
- Typical evidence we accept: current SOC 2 Type II report OR a signed attestation plus the last 12 months of security patch logs.

Laura — can you confirm the exact DPA language we want Cloudline to push to EdgeStream and whether we need to request a DocuSign addendum to the MSA/Order Form? Dev — can you flag if EdgeStream's described processing (SOW p.3) requires additional constraints (e.g., dedicated encryption keys, restricted access)?

Tessa Morgan
Vendor Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.inference <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>, dev.patel@redwood.inference <dev.patel@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Downstream vendor consent required for Cloudline integration

Tessa / team — reviewed the SOW and the matrix. Key legal ask list below (redlines I recommend):

1) Mandatory flow-down clauses to the subcontractor (EdgeStream):
   - Standard DPA flow-down: purpose limitation, no further subprocessing without consent, deletion/return at termination.
   - Incident notification: immediate verbal notice + written report within 72 hours.
   - Access controls: MFA for admin, least-privilege access, quarterly access reviews.

2) Audit & evidence:
   - Prefer SOC 2 Type II within last 12 months. If unavailable, accept: (a) independent security attestation signed by EdgeStream + (b) right to request specific logs for a defined investigation scope (limited to the telemetry artifacts described).
   - Reserve a right to perform on-site or remote audit with 30 days' notice for the first 12 months after go-live.

3) Contract mechanics:
   - Cloudline should provide a signed subprocessor addendum (simple DocuSign) confirming the flow-down to EdgeStream; a clause in the Order Form referencing the addendum is fine.
   - Include an explicit termination-for-convenience carve-out if EdgeStream materially breaches data obligations and Cloudline cannot remediate within 30 days.

Questions for Dev: is the telemetry data processed by EdgeStream purely aggregated/non-identifiable as described? If not, we need to escalate to Security for classification and potentially require encryption-at-rest with customer-specific KMS.

I'll prepare a short redline and attach a one-page addendum template we can send to Cloudline.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_subprocessor_addendum_template.docx (docx)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
To: Cloudline Partners <legal@cloudline.com>
Cc: Clara Hsu <clara.hsu@enterpriseco.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.inference <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, dev.patel@redwood.inference <dev.patel@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Required downstream consent & next steps (EdgeStream subcontractor)

Hi Cloudline legal team — thanks for flagging EdgeStream as a downstream processor. We're supportive of the integration but need to lock in a few items before we sign off. Summary of required items (per Redwood legal):

1) Subprocessor addendum: Please have Cloudline execute the attached Redwood Subprocessor Addendum with EdgeStream. Key items to include: DPA flow-down, 72-hour incident reporting, quarterly access review, and right to audit for the first 12 months.

2) Evidence: Provide either a current SOC 2 Type II report for EdgeStream OR the signed attestation + last 12 months of security patch logs. If EdgeStream cannot provide SOC 2, please confirm willingness to accept a limited remote audit.

3) Contract mechanics: Insert a reference to the executed subprocessor addendum in the Order Form (e.g., "Order Form Exhibit A — Subprocessor Addendum"). If EdgeStream later seeks to change subcontractors, Cloudline must notify Redwood and obtain our consent.

4) Timeline & link: We need the signed addendum and evidence by Oct 19, 2026 to keep the current go-live date. You can return the signed addendum via DocuSign link here: https://www.docusign.com/CLD-8421-sign.

If Cloudline prefers, we can send a redlined Order Form with the exact clause language and the addendum template attached.

Next steps for Redwood internal team: Laura will send the addendum template and a short redline to Cloudline if they want us to propose language; Dev will confirm whether aggregated telemetry requires any KMS separation (Laura + Dev please action).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Tessa Morgan
Vendor Partnerships
Redwood Inference
